limitations: Accepted present and fresh snapshot rates are application measurements, not physical scanout on the 60 Hz monitor.
Each process has three consecutive sample windows, not three independent launches; all included reruns and outliers are retained.
The generic 2250-unit rerun has a middle window with 256.9 ms p99 and reduced throughput; its cause remains unresolved and its data is included.

The final 741-unit run also has long-frame outliers. Repeating the unchanged old runtime reduces fresh throughput substantially; the current FPS variability prevents claiming a stable whole-application improvement.
Idle units retain normal simulation. Living counts remain 741 or 2250; visible counts and animation state can evolve with simulation rate.
These results are from the current Intel Iris Xe laptop and driver; native GPU behavior on other platforms and GPUs was not tested.
The repository replay-index integration test lacks local replay files; final core canvas tests and desktop tests pass, but the complete core suite is not all green.

Save-restore driver parity fails before and after at the same initial state offsets. Owner-session CPU harness waits for a presented resized camera without a GPU consumer and times out in both packages. These failures are not claimed resolved.
Recorded-replay full-state comparison and vanilla constructor/draw smoke pass; original-client network interoperability and exhaustive GPU visual equivalence are outside this verification.
Native Vulkan shutdown still reports retained allocations, also present in the baseline; normal exit does not establish warning-free cleanup.
